title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation [the process of becoming like Jesus] part 2
devotional:
Understanding Eden.

If you were to ask most Christians what they knew about the Garden of Eden you would probably get an answer something like ‘Eden was a garden where God placed Adam and Eve.’ That would be true, but incomplete. If I were to say to you that a television was a box that sits in the corner of the room, I would be telling the truth, but be saying nothing that would communicate what a television was. It’s the same with the Garden of Eden. The garden of Eden needs to be understood as a sacred space, as holy ground.

Notice that the creation story is told in a period of seven days. This is significant! In the ancient Israelites’ world, temples were always dedicated with a seven-day ceremony. This was true not only of the Israelites’ temple built for their God, but also of neighbouring nations’ temples which they raised for their deities. This ritual was so deeply ingrained in ancient culture that the Israelites would have immediately understood a seven-day creation story to mean that creation itself was a temple for their God.

The Garden was the unique place of God’s presence. Eden was the place where God walked back and forth with man, paralleled this with later references to the Tabernacle (Gen. 3:8 with Lev. 26:12, Deut. 23:14; 2 Sam. 7:6–7).

Ezekiel’s view of the Garden of Eden as the first sanctuary.

In Ezekiel 28:13–18 the prophet draws a number of parallels between Eden and Israel’s tabernacle/temple. Specifically, the prophet references Eden as a sanctuary and pictures Adam dressed as a priest (v. 13). And “Ezekiel 28:18 is probably therefore, the most explicit place anywhere in biblical literature where the Garden of Eden is called a temple” Genesis 2:15 says ‘’God placed Adam in the Garden ‘to cultivate (i.e., work] it and to keep it.’ The two Hebrew words for ‘cultivate and keep’ are usually translated ‘serve and guard [or keep]’ elsewhere in the Old Testament. It is true that the Hebrew word usually translated ‘cultivate’ can refer to an agricultural task when used by itself… When, however, these two words…occur together in the Old Testament…, they refer either to Israelites ‘serving’ God and ‘guarding [keeping]’ God’s word…or to priests who ‘keep’ the ‘service’ (or ‘charge’) of the tabernacle (see Num. 3:7-8; 8:25-26; 18:5-6; 1 Chr. 23:32; Ezek. 44:14).

Before we move on let us think about this. God originally place mankind in a sacred space, a place were they were able to worship God and have fellowship with him. We have been designed for ’temple life.’ to find our life through worship.

“God’s purpose in creating Adam and Eve is summed up in what they could do for God that nothing else in the whole creation could do. They had an exclusive on God, shared by no other of God’s creation.”

A.W. Tozer, goodreads.com. Accessed 22/05/2025

When Moses said that all mankind was made in the image of God, it would have been a very controversial statement in it’s day, because people believed and were taught that only those in positions of power and authority, like a king or a pharaoh, were made in the image of God, and to see a common slave as someone made in God’s image would have been revolutionary and unheard of.
prayer: Father thank you no matter what others think about us, or what we think about ourselves, our reality is that we have been made in the Image of God.
